summary: Provision Slack channel templates and cross-tenant claim-bot gateway for project onboarding
description:
Issue summary: Request to create a managed gateway that provisions Slack channel templates (team, project, incident-runbook templates) and a cross-tenant channel-claim bot that automates Confluence space seeding and a matching Jira project.

Impact: Currently new pods and external partner projects require manual channel creation, manual Confluence seeding, and hand-offs to Platform Ops. This slows onboarding and causes inconsistent RBAC and missing runbooks which increases security and incident readiness risk.

Goals: 1) Introduce a set of audited Slack channel templates with role mapping (owner, admin, writer, reader) that can be used by self-serve pod bootstrap. 2) Build a claim-bot that: validates requester identity, enforces guest/timebound access, creates a Confluence seed page(s) based on template, and optionally creates a zipped Jira project with templated issue types and board. 3) Provide a rollout/opt-in gating mechanism and audit log for security/compliance.

Stakeholders: Platform Onboarding, Security, Developer Experience, SRE, Legal (for partner guest flows).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) New pod requests Slack channel via admin form (manual today).
2) Platform Onboarding creates channel and assigns roles; sometimes misses runbook templates.
3) Confluence space is created separately or not at all; onboarding checklist incomplete.
4) Result: inconsistent permissions and missing incident preparedness artefacts.
logs: N/A - governance/operational request rather than a runtime error
Recent audit: 2026-01-30 channel onboarding sample showed 24% missing runbooks (internal audit spreadsheet link in related_confluence_pages).
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-02-10): Filing request after onboarding retrospective; asked for RBAC controls and auditability. See attached audit notes.

Marcus Li (2026-02-11): Can own design + initial automation. Will draft an architecture proposal and required IAM changes. Blocking: Confirmation of allowed guest domains and lifetime policy from Security.
Samir Khan - Security (2026-02-12): Prefer timebound guest access (default 7 days) with renewal flow; require pre-approved partner domain list. Need legal sign-off for partner data retention.

Priya Desai - DevEx (2026-02-16): Request templates should include incident-runbook channel and an 'ops-oncall' role mapping. Also request option to seed a sample Jira project with standard issue types for experiments.
investigation_notes: Reviewed existing automation: INT-912345 and INT-111222 show partial implementations of seeding but are tightly coupled to legacy bot. Reuse possible but needs RBAC overhaul.
Slack provisioning API rate limits acceptable for batched onboarding; however partner guest invites require SCIM/SCIM bridge validation and may need temporary elevated token for claim-bot flow.
Confluence seeding can use existing page templates; need a service account with page creation scope and audit logging enabled. Consider app credential rotation per INT-513210.
Risk assessment: Guest lifecycle and audit must meet security checklist; propose automated expiry and reminder emails to owners before expiry.
resolution: Partial: Architecture doc drafted and approved by Platform Onboarding and DevEx (see related_confluence_pages). Security provided guest lifetime policy and pre-approved domain list. Next: implement claim-bot prototype and a safe rollout to two internal pods for validation.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Build claim-bot prototype that performs: identity validation, channel creation from template, guest invite with expiry, Confluence seed page creation (assignee: Marcus Li).
2) Create Jira project seed job that can be toggled on/off in template (assignee: DevEx team).
3) Security to provide final partner domain list and legal sign-off on retention (assignee: Samir Khan).
4) QA run with two internal pods and produce onboarding metrics dashboard (assignee: SRE).
5) Create runbook for emergency manual takeover if claim-bot fails (assignee: Platform Oncall).
